To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a series of naphthalenimide based long wavelength fluorescence boronic acids that are useful for sensing carbohydrates.

we have synthesized a new family of boronic acid-based fluorescent reporters with long wavelength fluorescence and evaluated them under near physiological conditions, and have examined the mechanism of sugar binding to these compounds.
the fluorescence changes of the boronic acids are due to a combination of excited state proton transfer (ESPT) and photoinduced electron transfer (PET) processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, evaluation, and mechanism studies of naphthlimide-based fluorescent boronic acids.
the design of boronic acid-based fluorescent reporter compounds that can be used to monitor the binding of carbohydrates.
the development of a new class of fluorescent boronic acid reporters that are useful for the detection of sugars.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fluorescence of the naphthalimides is quenched by the formation of a boronate complex with a sugar.
the boronic acid moiety is not the main factor for the fluorescence enhancement observed in these compounds.
the observed fluorescence changes are due to the formation of a boronate anion, and that the boronate anions have different structures in the presence of different sugars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the naphthalimides are a good platform for boronic acid fluorescent reporters with long-wavelength emissions.
the boronic acids that are based on naphthalimides are very promising fluorescent reporters for sugars, with the potential to be applied to biological studies.

the boronic acids studied in this paper are useful long-wavelength fluorescent reporters for carbohydrates, and the fluorescence change upon carbohydrate binding is due to the formation of an intramolecular hydrogen-bonded complex between the boronic acid and the amino group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the boronic acid reporter compounds based on naphthalimides have great potential as long-wavelength fluorescent sensors for sugars.
the boronic acid group is the main contributor to the fluorescence change upon sugar binding.
the boronic acids in these compounds are able to undergo a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) reaction with the 4-amido group of naphthalene.
